title: Linear Algebra in Python: A Notebook Course in Matrices, Algorithms, and Learning
description:
A complete linear-algebra course in 55 executable notebooks: a Prologue, ten chapters (the machine, matrices, orthogonality, eigenvalues, the SVD, numerical linear algebra, structured matrices, tensors, the linear algebra of machine learning, and quantum information as linear algebra — through attention, LoRA, Tsirelson's bound and the quantum Fourier transform), and an Epilogue that closes the Prologue's question. Every notebook executes in CI with validation gates; roughly 1,100 checks distinguish what the mathematics determines from what the machine chooses.

Read the course at ramador.me/linear-algebra-in-python-public. This archive captures the runnable, solution-stripped public mirror. Text is licensed CC BY 4.0; code cells are MIT.
